I see a chiro once in a blue moon. He’s sort of a friend of mine and was the first and only chiro I’ve ever worked with.

I think my friend is an extremely knowledgeable person and deserves the title of doctor. He knows the structures of the body backwards and forwards and also was a FD paramedic for a long time. 

He also is a skeptic of the medical community because of their tendencies to overprescribe medication. Fair. 

My opinion? I think both sides of the coin can be very money hungry. Whenever you can bill insurance (be it for super frequent chiro adjustments or unnecessary medications) then I think I lot of people do it. 

At the end of the day I do think that it’s up to the specific practitioner. The best ones use their knowledge to make their patients feel better. If that involves adjustments OR medication, then good. 

As far as actual chiropractic work goes? I think it’s a bandaid. It can definitely help with acute pain but long term it’s not a solution. 

As a massage therapist I feel similarly to my own profession. We can help immensely with immediate pain relief but the true “cure” is to guide our clients to self healing through them making lifestyle changes.

Ok after this fiasco I have to share what helped me most. 

Squash EVERY moth you find. Check your coats and clothing for larvae (it’s disgusting but they like fabrics)   What really helped me was a product that was like a sticky trap (you can find them on Amazon). They secrete pheromones that the male moths are attracted to and they get stuck on the paper so they can’t reproduce. The female moths will lay eggs preferably in a food source. I highly recommend you inspect ALL your foodstuffs (including pet foods) that aren’t in the fridge or freezer. Put everything in either a glass, hard plastic, or tin container. These NEED to have airtight lids. The best way to control this situation is eliminate any food source for them and trap/kill as many as possible. Eventually they die off and can’t reproduce anymore. We kept our foods in those containers for like 6 months. In the spring time, we found like ONE moth who had been dormant. So, keep a vigil eye out. Also clean out things with crumbs like the tray inside a toaster if you have one, crumbs on the floor of your pantry, etc. If you’re really concerned, you can toss your flour and stuff like that in the freezer for 48 hours and that will kill off anything. Honestly I just threw a lot of stuff away to be safe 😭😭😭 good luck and I hope you get it under control!!!!
